provenance: Companies founded 2021-2026 where at least one founder was a Stanford student (undergrad, master's, PhD or postdoc) at or immediately before founding. Excludes founders who spent more than about five years in industry first, per the brief. Every figure was retrieved by web search on 2026-09-11 and is attributed. 'Backers' lists only investors named in a cited source. Where a claim could not be verified it is marked.

companies.name: Humans&
companies.founders: Eric Zelikman (Stanford CS PhD, then xAI) CEO; Noah Goodman (Stanford professor); Andi Peng (ex-Anthropic, worked on Claude 3.5-4.5 post-training); Yuchen He (ex-xAI); Georges Harik (Google employee #7)
companies.what: Human-centric AI lab; software for people to collaborate with each other and with models, including training models to ask the user for information and store it
companies.round: $480M seed at $4.48B, Jan 2026 — one of the largest seed rounds on record
companies.backers: NVIDIA, Jeff Bezos, GV, Emerson Collective, Forerunner, S32, DCVC, Human Capital, Felicis, CRV

companies.name: Simile
companies.founders: Joon Sung Park (Stanford CS PhD; creator of the 'Smallville' generative-agents study; Stanford's Arthur Samuel Award for best CS dissertation) CEO; Percy Liang (Stanford professor, CRFM director); Michael Bernstein (Stanford professor, HAI senior fellow)
companies.what: Simulating human behaviour at scale — 'agentic twins' of real consumers for market research
companies.round: $200M Series B at $2B led by Greenoaks, Aug 2026, five months after a $100M Series A
companies.backers: Sequoia, Greenoaks

companies.name: Axiom Math
companies.founders: Carina Hong — left her Stanford maths PhD in March 2026; MIT maths undergrad, Rhodes Scholar; aged 24-25 at founding
companies.what: An AI mathematician; verified reasoning systems aimed beyond probabilistic LLMs. Recruited researchers from Meta FAIR, Meta GenAI and Google Brain
companies.round: $64M seed, then $200M Series A at $1.6B — five months apart
companies.backers: Investor names not fully disclosed in retrieved sources

companies.name: Wispr Flow
companies.founders: Tanay Kothari (Stanford CS 2016-2020) CEO and Sahaj Garg (Stanford engineering; research assistant in the Stanford AI Lab with Andrew Ng) — Stanford batchmates who founded straight out of undergrad. Kothari had built a voice music platform at age 11 that reached 2.5M monthly users
companies.what: Voice dictation that replaces the keyboard; pivoted from a neural wearable to software
companies.round: $4.5M seed at founding; $2B valuation reported Aug 2026; $81M total over 6 rounds
companies.backers: NEA, 8VC

companies.name: Cartesia
companies.founders: Karan Goel CEO, Albert Gu (now CMU faculty), Arjun Desai, Brandon Yang — all four Stanford PhDs advised by Chris Ré, who co-founded with them. They founded on graduating in 2023
companies.what: Productising State Space Models, the architecture they invented in Ré's lab; Sonic real-time voice models
companies.round: $27M early, $64M Series A led by Kleiner Perkins, then a $100M round alongside the Sonic-3 launch
companies.backers: Kleiner Perkins, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA

companies.name: Engram
companies.founders: Dan Biderman (Stanford postdoc under Chris Ré; Columbia PhD) CEO; Sabri Eyuboglu (Stanford PhD under Ré, created Cartridges) CTO; Jessy Lin (Berkeley PhD, Meta FAIR); Jack Morris (Cornell PhD, FAIR); Scott Linderman (Stanford statistics/neuroscience professor); Chris Ré
companies.what: Enterprise AI memory layer; cutting token costs by turning document corpora into small reusable memories
companies.backers: General Catalyst

companies.name: Flapping Airplanes
companies.founders: Ben Spector (Stanford Statistics PhD; former North American debate champion; ran the Prod incubator that helped founders of Cursor, Decagon, Etched and Decart), his brother Asher Spector, and Aidan Smith (Thiel Fellow who worked at Neuralink for three years while at Georgia Tech). Aged 25, 26 and early 20s
companies.what: Foundational AI research lab attacking the data-efficiency problem
companies.round: $180M seed Jan 2026; reported in talks at $5B in July 2026
companies.backers: GV, Sequoia, Index Ventures, Lux Capital, Kleiner Perkins

companies.name: Pika
companies.founders: Demi Guo and Chenlin Meng — both dropped out of their Stanford AI Lab PhDs in April 2023. Guo has a Harvard maths BA and CS master's and an IOI silver medal. They met in the Stanford AI Lab and were provoked by a Runway AI film festival
companies.what: AI video generation and editing for non-professionals
companies.backers: Lightspeed Venture Partners, Factorial Capital

companies.name: Applied Compute
companies.founders: Rhythm Garg, Yash Patil (CEO) and Linden Li — Stanford grads (Li holds a Stanford BS and MS in CS, 2023), then roughly two years at OpenAI building o1, Codex and deep research. All 25 or under
companies.what: Custom reinforcement-learning models for enterprises; cheaper open-source alternative to frontier labs
companies.round: $20M at $100M pre-launch (Benchmark), $80M Series A at ~$700M, then reported talks at $1.3B
companies.backers: Benchmark, Sequoia, Lux Capital, Neo, Definition Capital, Hanabi Ventures; angels including Elad Gil

companies.name: Rox
companies.founders: Ishan Mukherjee (MIT M.Eng) CEO with Avanika Narayan (Stanford PhD student in Chris Ré's lab), Diogo Ribeiro, Shriram S and Chris Ré
companies.what: Agent swarms for enterprise sales teams, built on the lab's data-preparation research
companies.round: $50M across a Sequoia-led seed and a General Catalyst-led Series A; launched publicly Nov 2024
companies.backers: Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst

companies.name: Radical Numerics
companies.founders: Eric Nguyen (Stanford bioengineering PhD; Cornell MEng) CEO; Michael Poli (Stanford PhD) Chief AI Scientist; Armin Thomas (Stanford postdoc under Chris Ré) CTO; Stefano Massaroli (postdoc with Yoshua Bengio) President
companies.what: General biological intelligence — AI that reads, writes and designs DNA. Built Evo, the first model to read and write DNA at scale
companies.backers: Emergence Capital; scientific advisors include Chris Ré, George Church, Eric Horvitz and former Assistant Secretary of Defense Andrew Weber

companies.name: Valar Labs
companies.founders: Anirudh Joshi (CEO), Viswesh Krishna (CTO) and Damir Vrabac (COO) — met as researchers in Andrew Ng's Stanford AI Lab. Came through PearX S21
companies.what: AI reading digitised pathology slides to predict treatment response; first product Vesta, for bladder cancer BCG therapy
companies.round: $4.15M seed led by a16z Bio + Health, then a $22M Series A co-led by DCVC and a16z
companies.backers: a16z Bio + Health, DCVC, Pear VC

companies.name: Phylo
companies.founders: Kexin Huang (had just completed his Stanford CS PhD under Jure Leskovec) CEO and Yuanhao Qu (Stanford cancer biology PhD student), with Stanford faculty Jure Leskovec and Le Cong as scientific co-founders. They built Biomni, a popular open-source biomedical research agent
companies.what: Agentic AI for biology; Biomni Lab, an IDE for biomedical research
companies.backers: a16z and Menlo Ventures (co-led, via the Anthology fund linked to Anthropic)

companies.name: Numbers Station
companies.founders: Ines Chami (Stanford ICME PhD) Chief Scientist, Sen Wu (Stanford PhD) Chief Architect, Chris Aberger CEO, and Chris Ré. All met doing PhDs in the Stanford AI Lab
companies.what: Foundation models applied to data wrangling and the analytics stack
companies.round: $17.5M Series A, March 2023. Acquired by Alation in May 2025 at 18 people
companies.backers: Madrona Venture Group; angel investors including Lip-Bu Tan and Mark Nelson

companies.name: Vori
companies.founders: Brandon Hill (Stanford BA, former student body VP; third-generation grocer) CEO, Tremaine Kirkman (Stanford; previously founded Greo, YC S17; worked at the White House) and Robert Pinkerton (Stanford MS Space Systems Engineering; built vehicle systems at SpaceX and Lyft) CTO. The three met at Stanford
companies.what: Operating system and POS for independent grocery stores
companies.backers: Y Combinator, South Park Commons

companies.name: Human Behavior
companies.founders: Amogh Chaturvedi (20, left Stanford; had already sold a startup at 19), Skyler Ji (22) and Chirag Kawediya (22). They met in 2023 at a hacker house Chaturvedi organised after leaving Stanford
companies.what: Vision AI that watches session replays to explain online user behaviour — aimed at what Mixpanel and PostHog cannot do
companies.round: $5M seed, raised in two days, Sept 2025
companies.backers: Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Paul Graham, Vercel Ventures

companies.name: Known

companies.what: AI-voice-driven dating app
companies.backers: Not named in retrieved sources

companies.name: Phia

companies.what: AI shopping assistant for price comparison and markup detection
companies.backers: Kleiner Perkins; angels including Kris Jenner, Hailey Bieber and Michael Rubin

companies.name: Willow

companies.what: AI voice dictation, changing how people interact with computers
companies.backers: Y Combinator

companies.name: Golpo
companies.founders: Brothers Shraman and Shreyas Kar — began building it while at Stanford, then left
companies.what: Generates animated explainer videos from documents and prompts
companies.backers: Not named in retrieved sources

companies.name: Coframe
companies.founders: Josh Payne — Stanford BS, MS in CS (AI) and MBA. Previously co-founded Autograph and AccessBell (sold to Tata Group); created GPT-Migrate, briefly #1 on GitHub Trending. Guest lectures at Stanford on code generation

companies.backers: Khosla Ventures, Nat Friedman

companies.name: 10x Science
companies.founders: Founding team out of Carolyn Bertozzi's Nobel-laureate Stanford lab; includes a two-time YC founder. 47+ publications between them
companies.what: Frontier AI models with deep memory for understanding and engineering biology, starting with drug development
companies.backers: Y Combinator (founder is a 2x YC alum)

companies.name: Breakthrough Ventures
companies.founders: Roman Scott and Itbaan Nafi — Stanford students who ran campus Demo Days through 2024-25 first; Raihan Ahmed leads the accelerator
companies.what: A $2M accelerator for student founders, by student founders: up to $100K grants, Microsoft and NVIDIA compute credits, mentorship from Waymo CEO Tekedra Mawakana, $50K follow-on. Targets 100+ companies over three years, Demo Day at Stanford
companies.backers: Mayfield, Collide Capital, and Stanford founder alumni

entry_points.name: Stanford Venture Studio
entry_points.note: Admission is non-competitive — guaranteed to any Stanford student who submits the application form. 24/7 coworking, compute credits, mentoring, and mixers explicitly for founding-team formation. Recently expanded with dedicated AI labs giving student teams compute.

entry_points.name: StartX
entry_points.note: Zero equity, no fees. Reported $120B total portfolio valuation, average $42M raised per company; ~123 startups supported as of May 2026 with 5 unicorns and 32 exits; wider community 1,300 companies and 20 unicorns.

entry_points.name: Cardinal Ventures
entry_points.note: 10-week program run twice a year (fall and spring), 12-20 teams admitted, weekly speaker sessions and structured workshops.

entry_points.name: NFX FAST for Stanford
entry_points.note: Either a $150K discovery check on an uncapped SAFE, or a $1.5M-$3M pre-seed/seed for 15%. Application deadline 12 April. NFX partners Pete Flint, Anna Piñol and Valerie Osband Mahoney are Stanford alumni. NFX was first investor in Mammoth Biosciences, Arc, Jupiter, SESO — all Stanford.

entry_points.name: Pear Garage / Pear Dorm
entry_points.who: Engineering students at Stanford and Berkeley
entry_points.note: Pear VC runs Garage for Bay Area engineering students and Dorm for student builders; winning teams get a $100K uncapped SAFE and a fast-track PearX partner meeting. Pear was the seed investor in Valar Labs (PearX S21).

entry_points.name: Neo Scholars and Neo Residency
entry_points.note: Neo Scholars: ~30 students a year, $20K grant plus mentor network — every one of OpenAI's new-grad hires in a recent year was a Neo scholar. Neo Residency: 5-8 students get $40K no-strings to take a semester off. Neo backed Cursor and Applied Compute.

entry_points.name: Y Combinator Early Decision
entry_points.who: Students who want to finish their degree
entry_points.note: Launched Sept 2025: apply now, get funded the moment you are accepted, then do YC after graduation. In W26 Stanford had 22 founders in the batch (Berkeley 30, Harvard 18).

entry_points.name: Z Fellows
entry_points.who: Technical builders of any age, including students
entry_points.note: One-week intensive, optional $10K investment at a $1B valuation cap. Many Stanford and MIT students participate while still enrolled.

entry_points.name: a16z Speedrun
entry_points.note: Up to $1M plus $10M+ in credits, 12 weeks in San Francisco. Acceptance rate below 0.4%. Over $180M deployed to 150+ startups.

entry_points.name: Thiel Fellowship
entry_points.note: $250,000 over two years in the 2026 class (up from $200K in 2025 and $100K before). 2026 cohort: 12 founders from 7 countries, including a Stanford CS student who was an MTS at OpenAI on agent memory and a Stanford AI Lab researcher. Prior fellows founded Anthropic, Cognition, Etched, Figma, Mercor.

entry_points.name: Breakthrough Ventures
entry_points.note: Student-run. Up to $100K grants, Microsoft and NVIDIA compute, $50K follow-on, Demo Day at Stanford.

entry_points.name: AI for Healthcare Bootcamp (Stanford ML Group)
entry_points.note: Its alumni started Valar Labs (a16z, $26M) and Wispr AI ($2B). This is the single highest-yield student program found in this pass relative to its size.

entry_points.name: TreeHacks
entry_points.note: 12th annual edition in Feb 2026 awarded $500,000 in prizes, up from $200,000 in 2025. Sponsored by OpenAI, Google and Anthropic.

entry_points.name: Stanford Horizons
entry_points.note: Stanford robotics drone hackathon — the hardware-side counterpart to TreeHacks.

entry_points.name: DAF-Stanford AI Studio
entry_points.note: Department of the Air Force and Stanford joint studio. Context: Stanford's first defense-tech career fair drew 300 students, Stanford DEFCON drew 1,000+ attendees, and Stanford Women in National Security has 150+ members.

entry_points.name: BASES
entry_points.who: Undergrads, entry via Frosh Battalion in early fall
entry_points.note: Runs the $100K pitch competition; you can apply to help run programs at the end of the school year.

entry_points.name: ASES
entry_points.note: 12-week design-thinking bootcamp for freshmen culminating in a pitch to Silicon Valley investors.

entry_points.name: Stanford Biotechnology Group / Students in Biodesign / SPARK
entry_points.note: The bio equivalents of the CS entry points; SPARK runs the translational-medicine startup pipeline.
